claims.statement: PEG-MGF is a pegylated synthetic analog of the mechano growth factor (MGF/IGF-1Ec) peptide, a splice variant isoform of insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1); published preclinical literature describes native MGF expression as exercise- and age-dependent, distinguishing it from the liver-derived, circulating IGF-1Ea isoform.

extractedEvidence.quote: the expression of Mechano Growth Factor (MGF), a member of the IGF-1 (insulin-like Growth Factor 1) super family, has been shown to be both exercise and age dependent.

reviewFlags: mechanism description is for the parent MGF/MGF-E peptide studied in the literature, not for the pegylated commercial analog itself, which has not been independently characterized in peer-reviewed sources located this pass

claims.statement: The available human-relevant evidence on the MGF/MGF-E peptide family is limited to conflicting in vitro cell-culture studies, not human clinical trials: one study found MGF-E significantly increased proliferative lifespan and fusion of satellite cells from neonatal/young-adult (but not old-adult) donors, while a separate study found the MGF C-terminal peptide (up to 500 ng/mL) failed to increase proliferation of C2C12 cells or primary human skeletal muscle myoblasts and failed to affect primary muscle stem cells, concluding this calls into question whether MGF has a physiological role at all. No published human clinical trial of PEG-MGF (the pegylated analog actually sold as a research/gray-market product) was located.

conflicts.summary: Two independent in vitro studies of the (unpegylated) MGF/MGF-E peptide reach opposite conclusions on human muscle-cell activity: Mavrommatis et al. (2011) report MGF-E significantly increases satellite-cell proliferative lifespan and fusion in younger donors, while Hill et al. (2014, Am J Physiol Endocrinol Metab) report no proliferative or differentiation effect on C2C12 cells or primary human myoblasts at concentrations up to 500 ng/mL and question whether MGF has any physiological role. No study on the pegylated commercial analog (PEG-MGF) was located to help adjudicate.

reviewReasons: Expansion-batch evidence packet requires human review before publication.

No PubChem/DrugBank/ChEMBL/CAS/UNII identifiers could be resolved for PEG-MGF this pass; PubChem's own search UI is JavaScript-rendered and PMC article pages returned reCAPTCHA challenges, blocking structured-database and additional literature fetches.
Directly conflicting in vitro findings (Mavrommatis 2011 vs. Hill 2014) on the parent MGF/MGF-E peptide remain unresolved and unadjudicated by any systematic review located this pass.

No PEG-MGF-specific (pegylated form) human or animal study was located; all literature evidence pertains to the unpegylated MGF/MGF-E research peptide, an extrapolation that should be re-examined by a reviewer.

FDA's PEG-MGF entry sits under a withdrawn nomination, not an active Category 1/2 determination; the compounding-eligibility and safety-risk status should be reconfirmed against FDA's live page at review time.
